title: col_add_str converted to col_set_str on a non-literal val_to_str default string
live_proof: absent at the 4.6.8 pin by inspection: packet-qnet6.c uses col_add_str at the site. The pre-fix shape is quoted from b48759e4a4^ at packet-qnet6.c:4066; the introducing conversion 9e3e17136c and the fix are both in v4.3.1.
object: the formatted default string of val_to_str, 70 bytes in wmem_packet_scope()
lifetime_ender: wmem_leave_packet_scope at the end of epan_dissect_run_with_taps (epan.c:665 at the fix's parent), before the packet is printed
shape: packet-scope object held by a column or address past the scope's end
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator; the seam's packet pool stands in for the separate wmem_packet_scope() pool, the same allocator type with the same reset
distinguishing: the only case whose fix is on the store side (copy into the column) rather than on the allocation's scope; introduced and fixed within one release by a mass conversion that mistook a heap string for a literal

native-detect.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-asan/: **NO ASan REPORT** on the buggy arm, which printed VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, so the defective access ran and ASan did not see it. The fixed arm exits 0 with VERDICT FIXED and no report. Built with the port's own allocator library under the same sanitizer (cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0; -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g -O0; wmem and the port built with the same flags). Positive controls in the same run: `asan-control past 402653184` -> heap-buffer-overflow; `asan-control uaf 402653184` -> heap-use-after-free -- so ASan reports on a heap block the size of this corpus's arena, and the silence is the arena: one malloc'd block, carved and recycled without free(). Predicted before the run (b64cd18b85d0); the arm was previously 'not written'.
native-detect.measured: 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-native-asan-libc/run-asan.txt: SILENT, the defect reproduced; wmem built with WM_LIBC_SYSTEM=ON (g_malloc/g_free are the host's malloc/free); wmem's own control 90 reported heap-use-after-free at wm_probe in the same run. The earlier reading (2026-10-09) ran the hosted bump arena, which could read nothing else.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-cheribsd-libc/: **NOT CAUGHT** on stock wmem with the system allocator as CheriBSD's libc (WM_LIBC_SYSTEM, WM_CHUNKS=OFF), revocation on: the buggy arm's reoccupation assertion held -- the stale chunk was REISSUED inside the block wmem kept, so libc's quarantine never saw it (missed, reused); fixed arm VERDICT FIXED. In the same boot control 90 (a jumbo g_free'd by the reset) was HELD by the quarantine and the revocation control faulted at its labelled load. The 2026-10-07 reading of this arm ran the hosted bump arena with the chunk port compiled in, where nothing reached free().
cheribsd-revocation.control: in the same boot (results/2026-10-10-cheribsd-libc/, provenance.tsv): the revocation control faulted at its labelled load (exit 162), the bounds control exited 162, and wmem's own control 90 -- a jumbo the reset hands to g_free, the one wmem path that does reach free() -- was HELD by libc's quarantine. So revocation was live and wmem traffic that reaches free() is seen; the completion here is a measured miss, not an absent integration. (The PoisonCap mode-1 13/13 this field used to cite is results/20260921-cheribsd/, a different bundle.)

native-fix-differential.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-differential/: the buggy sequence reaches storage outside its object (VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, exit 0) and the fixed sequence -- this case's upstream fix, modelled in case.c under wm_fixed -- does not (VERDICT FIXED, exit 0). Hosted build, upstream wmem allocator (WM_CHUNKS=OFF), `program 0 N buggy|fixed` (runners/run-native.sh). Temporal: the next dissection reoccupies the freed storage, asserted to be the same address, and the stale read returns its marker. The arm did not exist before 2026-10-09: the cases had no fixed sequence.
